quote: advance in line of battle through a wheat-field, his left resting on the woods which skirted the field
says: On the afternoon of 2 July the Wheatfield was in wheat and Cross's brigade advanced through it in line with its left on the woods.
note: Caldwell's own report (Second Corps, First Division).

quote: The brigade steadily drove the enemy back to the far end of the wheat-field, a distance of over 400 yards
says: The wheat-field the Third Brigade crossed was more than 400 yards (366 m) long on the line of advance.
note: Used as a size check on the outline of the field (about 20 acres), not to move the outline.

quote: Both brigades advanced in line of battle through a wheat-field into a wood
says: The brigades of Kelly and Zook advanced through a wheat-field into a wood in the evening of 2 July.

quote: moved forward in order of battle through a wheat-field, about the center of which we commenced firing, continuing for fifteen minutes or more
says: A regiment of Brooke's brigade fought for fifteen minutes or more in the middle of the wheat-field.

quote: In passing back over the wheat-field, I found the enemy had nearly closed in my rear
says: Brooke's brigade crossed the wheat-field twice in the fight of 2 July.

quote: crossed a low marshy ground in front to a wheat-field lying between two thick belts of woods beyond
says: Between the Fifth Corps' line and the wheat-field lay low marshy ground (the Plum Run bottom), and the wheat-field lay between two thick belts of woods.
feature: Plum Run bottom and Rose Wheatfield
note: Crawford's report of the evening of 2 July.

quote: Beyond this lay two thick masses of timber, separated by a large wheat-field
says: Two thick masses of timber stood on either side of the large wheat-field.

quote: in a small wheat-field near the base of Round Top hill
says: Winslow's battery stood in a small wheat-field near the foot of Round Top on the afternoon of 2 July.
note: Not placed: the report gives no distance or bearing.

quote: form a line across a small wheat-field on my left, to connect two brigades
says: Burling's brigade was ordered to form across a small wheat-field on the afternoon of 2 July.
feature: small wheat-field of the Third Corps' left

quote: established a battery of ten guns (four 20-pounders and six 10-pounder Parrotts) in a wheat-field to the north and a little to the east of the Cemetery Hill
says: A Confederate battery stood in a wheat-field north and a little east of Cemetery Hill at about 15:30 on 2 July (Benner's Hill).
note: Hunt's report; the field is east of the town, 1,200 to 1,300 yards from Cemetery Hill. Not placed: the repository holds no coordinates for Benner's Hill.

quote: they planted a battery of four 20-pounders and six 10-pounder Parrotts in a wheat-field on our immediate front, at about 1,300 yards
says: The same Confederate battery stood in a wheat-field about 1,300 yards in front of Wainwright's guns.

quote: to the right of the Baltimore pike, in a field of wheat
says: On the morning of 2 July a battery of the Sixth Corps stood in a field of wheat to the right of the Baltimore Pike.

quote: which took post in an oat-field, about 380 yards south of the Cashtown road
says: On 1 July Cooper's battery took post in an oat-field on Seminary Ridge about 380 yards south of the Cashtown (Chambersburg) road.
note: Anchor: 380 yards (347 m) south of the road at the Seminary. The position of the road line at that point is taken from the repository's road layer; the anchor radius covers that and the 30-40 m error of the outlines.

quote: the battery being posted in an oat-field some 350 yards south of the Cashtown road
says: Wainwright confirms the oat-field on Seminary Ridge, about 350 yards south of the Cashtown road, on 1 July.

quote: our line advanced up the slope and deployed in the oat-field, some 15 rods from the pike
says: On 2 July a regiment of Graham's brigade deployed in an oat-field about 15 rods (75 m) from the Emmitsburg pike, beside the Peach Orchard.
note: The anchor is the Sherfy farmstead (the Peach Orchard); the NPS inventory puts the Sherfy oats in the eastern field (see VC-NPSX-CLI-PCB-p082-04).

quote: While lying down in a clover-field
says: On the evening of 2 July the Regulars of the Fifth Corps lay down in a clover-field where the enemy opened with artillery.
feature: clover-field of the Fifth Corps' left
note: Not placed: the report names no landmark.

quote: on each side of which was an open corn-field
says: On 2 July a wood stood between two open corn-fields on the Union left.
feature: corn-fields beside a wood, Union left

quote: the regiment finally arrived at a corn-field, where the battle had been already raging for several hours
says: A Fifth Corps regiment arrived at a corn-field where the battle had raged for several hours (2 July).

quote: undulating, here arid there covered with grain, and a small woods extended across it
says: On 1 July the ground north of the town where Schurz's division fought was undulating, in places in grain, with a small wood across it.
feature: fields north of the town (Barlow's Knoll side)

quote: The bivouac was necessarily in a wheat-field, the stacks of which the men slept on, which were thus trampled considerably
says: On the night of 9 to 10 July wheat in the field at the Boonsborough and Williamsport turnpike (Maryland) was already cut and stacked, and the stacks were trampled by a division.
feature: wheat harvest in Washington County, Maryland

about.region: Washington County, Maryland, about 35 miles south-west

note: Prince's own report. The field is not near Gettysburg; it dates a harvest in the same agricultural region and the same season.

quote: subsisted entirely on wheat and grass, or new hay
says: From 10 to 25 July horses at Downsville, Maryland, were fed cut wheat, grass and new hay.
feature: hay and wheat harvest in Maryland
note: Report of a Confederate artillery officer.

quote: I extended my right by moving the Seventeenth Maine Volunteers, Lieutenant-Colonel Merrill commanding, across a wheat
says: De Trobriand sent the 17th Maine across a wheat field on 2 July.
